threatModelSummary: This change wires a local/CI shell script (scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh) to an already-verified container image to run a Playwright suite in real Chrome under Xvfb. There is no authentication, authorization, API surface, user-supplied input, or secret handling introduced. The one named trust boundary — the VNC viewer must stay off and never print its password — is satisfied structurally: the script never sets or references RUNNER_VIEWER, and docker run only forwards RUNNER_SLOW_MO/RUNNER_VIDEO into the container, so the viewer stays unset regardless of the host environment. All docker-exec payloads use fixed, non-interpolated command strings; the only variables passed through (RUNNER_SLOW_MO, RUNNER_VIDEO, CONTAINER_NAME via $$) are quoted and never built from untrusted input. No new dependencies were added. Two residual observations are recorded below as Low/Info — neither blocks QA.
dependencyAudit: No new dependencies introduced by this change (implementation-notes.md confirms 'Dependencies Added: None') — pnpm audit was not run since there is nothing new to audit.

stride.assessed: No authentication, session, or identity surface exists in this script or the test files it adds; nothing to spoof.

docker exec payloads are fixed command strings, not built from untrusted input. RUNNER_SLOW_MO/RUNNER_VIDEO pass through quoted docker -e flags and are consumed via Number()/strict-equality checks in playwright.config.ts, not shell-interpolated. pnpm install uses --frozen-lockfile, preventing silent lockfile drift.
Local/CI dev tooling with no user-attributable actions to audit; not applicable at this layer.

Checked whether the VNC viewer or its password could leak — RUNNER_VIEWER is never set or referenced by this script, satisfying the spec's trust boundary. Checked the app.log tail printed on health-check failure (wait_for_app_healthy) — apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/.env contains no secrets today, only non-sensitive dev flags, so the tail cannot currently disclose credentials; flagged as Info for future-proofing. Checked outbound destinations — none are introduced; the container's own network egress is a pre-existing, out-of-scope image property, not something this diff changes.

wait_for_app_healthy is bounded by the named APP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (180s) constant with curl --max-time 5 per probe, matching the NFR, and exits a distinct non-zero code (EXIT_APP_UNHEALTHY) rather than hanging. No unbounded loops over user-controlled data exist in this script.

Container runs as non-root USER runner (containers/saturday-runner/Containerfile, unmodified, out of scope). docker run uses no --privileged, no extra capabilities, and no host network/PID namespace sharing. The repo bind-mount (-v REPO_ROOT:/work) gives the container write access to the checkout, which is the intended, expected behavior of a local test runner the developer already chose to execute, not a privilege boundary this diff crosses.

findings.title: Container network egress is not structurally restricted during the suite run
findings.description: docker run uses the default bridge network rather than --network=none or an egress allowlist. The spec's NFR states the app and mock API make no request off the container after dependencies are installed, but that is an application-behavior assumption, not a network-policy guarantee — a compromised dependency pulled during pnpm install, or a regression in the app/mock-api, could reach the network undetected. This is a pre-existing property of how the runner image and this script are used together, not something this diff newly introduces, and restricting it would require reconfiguring container networking per-phase (install vs. test), which is an architectural change outside this spec's scope (containers/saturday-runner/ is explicitly out of scope).
findings.verification: Not applicable — no fix applied; recorded as a defense-in-depth gap for a human to weigh, not blocking QA.

findings.title: Health-check failure path dumps the app's dev-server log verbatim to stderr
findings.description: On timeout, the script runs `tail -n 50 /tmp/app.log` and prints it to stderr. Today apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/.env carries only non-sensitive dev flags (ENABLE_OTEL, OTEL endpoint, HEADLESS, BROWSER, ENVIRONMENT), so there is nothing sensitive to leak. If a secret is ever added to that .env or logged by the dev server, this tail would surface it in CI console output. No action needed now; worth a one-line note for whoever next touches this script's error path.

notesForQa: No Critical or High findings — nothing blocks QA from proceeding.

Two Low/Info findings recorded for awareness only: (1) container network egress isn't structurally blocked during the run, it relies on the app/mock-api not making outbound calls, matching the NFR as a behavioral assertion QA can verify but not a technical guarantee; (2) the health-check failure path tails and prints /tmp/app.log to stderr, which is safe today because .env has no secrets, but would need redaction if that ever changes.
